rgb: The setting is an unfinished interior with grey plastered walls, a tall ceiling, and a raised bamboo scaffolding platform spanning the room over a sunlit floor. In frames 1, 2, and 5, the camera wearer gazes upward at the scaffolding approximately 2.5 to 4 metres away and overhead, where a man wearing a patterned shirt, blue jeans, and a cap stands on the central bamboo poles, facing and watching the camera wearer while holding a small yellow tool. Another person, dressed in a pink shirt and jeans, stands around 1.5 to 2 metres to his right, nearer the foreground at the right edge and roughly 2 metres from the camera wearer, facing away toward the right wall and partially cut off by the frame's right boundary. A plastering float lies on the lower-left bamboo poles about 1 to 1.5 metres in front of the wearer. In frame 2, a rectangular block is airborne immediately right of the central man, while in frame 5 the yellow tool is in mid-air just above his lifted hands and within his arm's reach. In frame 3, the camera wearer sharply angles their head downward toward the floor and lower scaffolding directly ahead and below. A black rectangular bucket, a mortar pan on the right, and a white circular pan are within arm's reach, about 0.5 to 1.5 metres away, while a blue basin is farther forward on the floor, around 2 to 2.5 metres away, beside the camera wearer's cast shadow. In frame 4, the wearer raises their head toward the underside and leading edge of the bamboo scaffolding about 1 to 3 metres ahead and overhead, with the blue basin still visible below on the left and the upper room concealed by dark shadow, then returns in frame 5 to looking upward at the man on the scaffolding.
depth: The depth map depicts the vertical arrangement of an indoor construction area containing multi-level bamboo scaffolding as the camera wearer changes head pitch from an upward view in frames 1–2, sharply down toward the floor in frame 3, across the middle-height poles in frame 4, and upward again in frame 5. In frames 1, 2, and 5, bright foreground readings position the lower scaffolding poles and a plastering trowel within or close to the wearer's arm's reach, 0.5–1.5 m below and ahead. Above, a partly cropped worker at the right is ~2–2.5 m away and faces left/away, while another worker occupies upper poles ~1.5–2 m farther back and left at ~3.5–4.5 m, facing right and looking down in frames 1–2 before looking upward in frame 5 with a brick inside his overhead reach. When the camera points down in frame 3, the map places a rectangular bucket and circular pans on the floor ~1–2.5 m below, with the closest container and poles near arm's reach. It then tilts upward in frame 4, revealing horizontal scaffolding ~1–2 m ahead. Importantly, in the heavily underexposed fourth frame, the depth map exposes the complete 3D structure of the mid-level bamboo poles and the faint outline of the distant standing worker ~3.5–4 m above, both nearly imperceptible in RGB alone. Its output is nevertheless unreliable because it entirely omits the airborne block near the distant worker's reach in frame 2, fuses slim openings between neighboring bamboo poles, and treats flat floor shadows and dark basins in frame 3 as separate depth surfaces.
segmentation: Against a black background, the segmentation map extracts only people and leaves out the walls, bamboo scaffolding, floor vessels, and bricks throughout all five frames. In frames 1 and 2, it marks the distant worker positioned above and left, ~3.5–4.5 m from the camera wearer, facing right and looking downward toward the wearer's direction with his arms extended in front and within reach of a brick. It also identifies the nearer worker standing ~1.5–2 m to his right and ~2–2.5 m from the wearer, facing away/left, with his right side and upper torso partly blocked by the right edge of the frame. As the camera wearer directs their head sharply down in frame 3, upward through the dark middle area in frame 4, and back toward the upper scaffolding in frame 5, both workers leave and then return to view while staying on their individual perches. In frames 1–2, the masks clearly distinguish the silhouette of the nearer right-side worker from the wall behind him, although the map is very unreliable in general. Between frames 1 and 2, it reverses the two workers' instance colours; in frame 3, it incorrectly classifies the camera wearer's flat shadow on the ground and a neighboring round pan ~1.5–2 m below as a person; and in frames 4 and 5, it entirely misses the distant worker reaching above his head as well as the lower leg of the worker on the right.
pose: The pose map displays sparse yellow 2D body skeletons over black, with no environmental geometry, objects, or nearer foreground people shown. It recognizes the distant worker on the upper-left scaffolding, ~3.5–4.5 m away and above the camera wearer and ~1.5–2 m left of the closer worker, only in frames 2 and 5. In frame 2, the worker faces right and looks downward toward the camera wearer/right; in frame 5, his head and both elevated arms turn upward within reach of a brick moving through the air. Over the sequence, while the camera points down in frame 3, rises through the dark scaffolding in frame 4, and returns toward the ceiling in frame 5, the map follows the distant worker's change from a stance with lowered arms to an overhead catching pose. The yellow skeletal connections in frame 5 cleanly distinguish the precise bends of his raised wrists and elbows against the poorly lit ceiling, details that are more difficult to interpret in RGB. The map remains unreliable, however: it does not detect the distant worker in frames 1 or 4, entirely overlooks the partly cropped right-side worker ~2–2.5 m away in frames 1, 2, and 5, finds no magenta hand skeletons on any person, and invents a head-and-torso skeleton over the camera wearer's flat 2D floor shadow ~1.5–2 m below in frame 3.
